# Lightbox

Thumbnails that open a full-screen image viewer. Use it for proof screenshots, a listing's photos or before-and-after pairs: pressing a thumbnail opens the viewer on that image. It shows the image as large as the screen allows, uncropped, with its title and caption under it and Close beside the position ("2 of 4") at its top. Step through the images with the arrow keys, the Previous and Next buttons, a trackpad or a swipe; the new position is announced politely, once. Escape, Close or a press outside closes it, and focus goes back to the thumbnail that opened it. The viewer grows from that thumbnail and slides between images; with reduced motion it fades and jumps instead.

```tsx
import { Lightbox } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/lightbox/lightbox";
```

## Example

```tsx
<Lightbox
  label="Kitchen photos"
  images={[
    { src: "/photos/before.jpg", alt: "The old kitchen, with dark cabinets", title: "Before" },
    { src: "/photos/after.jpg", alt: "The new kitchen, with white cabinets", title: "After", caption: "Six weeks later" },
  ]}
/>
```

## Use instead when

- Use `Carousel` instead to show the images in the page one at a time, and `Dialog` when the viewer holds more than images.

## Props

Type: `LightboxProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: width and margins (`max-w-2xl`, `mt-6`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `closeLabel` | `string` | `"Close"` | The close button's accessible name. |
| `images` (required) | `readonly LightboxImage[]` |  | The images, in order. The thumbnails show them in a grid, and the viewer steps through them. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | Names the thumbnails and the viewer for screen readers, and shows at the viewer's top, such as "Kitchen photos". It is always required. |
| `loop` | `boolean` |  | Next on the last image goes back to the first, and Previous on the first goes to the last. |
| `nextLabel` | `string` | `"Next image"` | The Next button's accessible name. |
| `originalLabel` | `string` | `"Open original"` | The text of the link to an image's `href`. |
| `positionLabel` | `string` | `"{n} of {total}"` | The position the viewer shows and announces when it changes: `{n}` is the image's number and `{total}` the number of images. |
| `previousLabel` | `string` | `"Previous image"` | The Previous button's accessible name. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `slides`: Not a prop. Pass the images as `images`: `<Lightbox images={[{ src, alt }]}>`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`).

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.

## Types

### `LightboxImage`

One image in a `Lightbox`.

```ts
interface LightboxImage {
  /** The full-size image's address, shown in the viewer. */
  src: string;
  /** Describes the image for screen readers, on its thumbnail and in the viewer. */
  alt: string;
  /** A smaller file for the thumbnail. @default src */
  thumbnail?: string | undefined;
  /** A short title under the image in the viewer, shown as given. */
  title?: ReactNode;
  /**
   * A line under the title in the viewer, shown as given: Lightbox adds nothing to it.
   */
  caption?: ReactNode;
  /** The original file, or a page about the image: the viewer links to it in a new tab. */
  href?: string | undefined;
}
```
